number_of_offences: Charged under 304B IPC, upheld under 306 IPC
key_evidence_accepted: It is established from ocular and documentary evidence that deceased was subjected to cruelty and harassment by respondent - As a result of such treatment of cruelty and harassment, she was driven to meet the suicidal death.
witness_credibility: Jugal Kishore (PW.1) and Simla Devi (PW.7) made ominous statements regarding demand of dowry that after the marriage demand of dowry was made by the in-laws. It is not made specific as to whether respondent demanded dowry.

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Section 304B IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment
appeal_history.high_court: Converted conviction to Section 306 IPC, reduced sentence to five years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/-

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased died within 7 years of her marriage under unnatural circumstances and that the respondent did not inform the parents of the deceased regarding the incident. The burden to prove innocence lies on the respondent after the prosecution has proved that the deceased died under unnatural circumstances within seven years of marriage.
defence_argument: The defence supported the decision rendered by the High Court, which converted the conviction from Section 304B IPC to 306 IPC and reduced the sentence from life imprisonment to five years imprisonment.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the main ingredient of the offence under Section 304B IPC is whether the deceased was subjected to cruelty and harassment by her husband, 'for or in connection with demand of dowry', soon before her death. The Court also applied the presumption under Section 113A of the Indian Evidence Act regarding abetment of suicide by a married woman.
precedent_relied_upon: Section 113A and 1138 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872; Section 304B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the High Court's determination that the deceased was subjected to cruelty and harassment, leading to her suicidal death, and that the accused had abetted her suicide, thus warranting conviction under Section 306 IPC.
